newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cathay seeks better flight punctuality.
newsitem.headline: Cathay seeks better flight punctuality.

text.p: Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd has introduced a quarterly On Time Performance(OTP) report to try and improve flight punctuality, the airline's in-house newspaper said.

Cathay's Service Delivery Improvement and On Time Performance manager, Peter Li, said the new report will keep managers up to date on how each port is performing in relation to others on Cathay's network.
Cathay passengers tend to accept delays out Kai Tak but not at other ports, Li said.

Cathay's home base is notoriously congested and Cathay has said departure delays rose to 61 per cent of all flights from Hong Kong in 1996 compared to 48 per cent in 1995. Slot availability, tight crew scheduling and high utilisation of Cathay's new fleet aircraft are other factors affecting OTP, Cathay said.
"We have to keep OTP to the forefront of everyone's mind if we want to improve," Li said.
Two of Cathay's less busy ports, Surabaya in Indonesia and Toronto, Canada have the highest OTP performance.
Taipei had the most catch-up minutes to deal with. Cathay said that means a flight touches down at its scheduled departure time or later and it is turned round with great speed on a regular basis.
"Taipei staff are the stars really, but Bangkok and Narita are also very important in helping us with OTP," Li said. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom -Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
